corrections.supersedes: Original Batch 06 release decision for this skill.
evidence: SKILL.md:157 labels the value a symmetric data encryption key (DEK).
SKILL.md:159 uses `let dek = random::<u32>().to_le_bytes().to_vec();`; u32 is 32 bits and to_le_bytes() returns exactly four bytes.
SKILL.md:161-170 immediately wraps those bytes with the RSA KEK, so the value is presented as the DEK in the claimed envelope-encryption workflow.
NIST FIPS 197 §6.1 permits AES key lengths of 128, 192, or 256 bits; 32 bits is not a valid AES key.
Microsoft Learn Azure data-encryption-at-rest guidance describes the DEK in its envelope-encryption hierarchy as a symmetric AES-256 key.
The example is therefore unusable as an AES DEK as written and can mislead an agent/user into deploying only 32 bits of purported encryption-key material.

primary_guidance.source: Microsoft Learn, Azure data encryption at rest — envelope encryption with a key hierarchy
primary_guidance.finding: Azure describes the DEK in this model as a symmetric AES-256 key.

corrections.remediation: Keep this individual skill on hold without modifying vendored upstream bytes. Re-review a corrected immutable upstream artifact before release.
